017package org.apache.juneau.rest.client;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.AssertionUtils.*;
020import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.Shorts.*;
021
022import java.io.*;
023import java.nio.charset.*;
024
025import org.apache.juneau.http.response.*;
026import org.apache.juneau.marshall.parser.*;
027import org.apache.juneau.marshall.sse.*;
028import org.apache.juneau.marshall.stream.*;
029
030/**
031 * A fluent accessor for an HTTP response body returned by {@link RestResponse}.
032 *
033 * <p>
034 * Provides convenient methods for reading the body as a string, byte array, or stream.
035 * The body is read lazily; each method reads and returns the body content once.
036 *
037 * <p>
038 * Obtain instances via {@link RestResponse#body()}.
039 *
040 * <p>
041 * <b>Beta — API subject to change:</b> This type is part of the next-generation REST client and HTTP stack
042 * ({@code org.apache.juneau.marshall.ng.*}).
043 * It is not API-frozen: binary- and source-incompatible changes may appear in the <b>next major</b> Juneau release
044 * (and possibly earlier).
045 *
046 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
047 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/NextGenRestClient">juneau-ng REST client</a>
048 * </ul>
049 *
050 * @since 9.2.1
051 */
052@SuppressWarnings({
053   "resource" // Eclipse resource analysis: response is borrowed; caller closes it after reading body
054})
055public final class ResponseBody {
056
057   private final RestResponse response;
058
059   ResponseBody(RestResponse response) {
060      this.response = response;
061   }
062
063   /**
064    * Returns the response body as a UTF-8 string.
065    *
066    * @return The body string, or <jk>null</jk> if the response has no body.
067    * @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs reading the body.
068    */
069   public String asString() throws IOException {
070      return response.getBodyAsString();
071   }
072
073   /**
074    * Returns the response body decoded with the given charset.
075    *
076    * @param charset The character set to use for decoding. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
077    * @return The body string, or <jk>null</jk> if the response has no body.
078    * @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs reading the body.
079    */
080   public String asString(Charset charset) throws IOException {
081      var stream = response.getBodyStream();
082      if (stream == null)
083         return null;
084      return new String(stream.readAllBytes(), charset);
085   }
086
087   /**
088    * Returns the response body as a byte array.
089    *
090    * @return The body bytes, or <jk>null</jk> if the response has no body.
091    * @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs reading the body.
092    */
093   @SuppressWarnings({
094      "java:S1168" // 'null' is a documented sentinel distinguishing 'no response body' (e.g. HTTP 204) from an empty body; callers rely on it (see RestClientFeatures_Test.l04_responseBody_nullBody).
095   })
096   public byte[] asBytes() throws IOException {
097      var stream = response.getBodyStream();
098      if (stream == null)
099         return null;
100      return stream.readAllBytes();
101   }
102
103   /**
104    * Returns the raw response body stream.
105    *
106    * <p>
107    * Callers should not close this stream directly; close the parent {@link RestResponse} instead.
108    *
109    * @return The body stream, or <jk>null</jk> if the response has no body.
110    */
111   public InputStream asStream() {
112      return response.getBodyStream();
113   }
114
115   /**
116    * Reads the response body into a byte array and returns it, or returns {@code null} if there is no body.
117    *
118    * <p>
119    * Equivalent to {@link #asBytes()}.
120    *
121    * @return The body bytes, or <jk>null</jk> if the response has no body.
122    * @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs reading the body.
123    */
124   public byte[] readAllBytes() throws IOException {
125      return asBytes();
126   }
127
128   /**
129    * Opens a token/record-streaming cursor over the response body using the parser negotiated from the response
130    * {@code Content-Type}.
131    *
132    * <p>
133    * Equivalent to {@link #asCursor(Parser, Class) asCursor(negotiatedParser, type)} where the parser is selected
134    * from the response {@code Content-Type} header; when no registered parser matches and no default parser is
135    * configured, a <c>415 Unsupported Media Type</c> is thrown.  Use {@link #asCursor(Parser, Class)} to read with an
136    * explicit parser.
137    *
138    * @param <T> The cursor type ({@link RecordReader}, {@link TokenReader}, or a concrete subtype).
139    * @param type The declared cursor type. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
140    * @return A cursor over the live response body. Never <jk>null</jk>.
141    * @throws IOException If the body is missing, the parser does not support the requested cursor surface, or the
142    *    produced cursor is not assignable to {@code type}.
143    */
144   public <T> T asCursor(Class<T> type) throws IOException {
145      return asCursor(negotiatedParser(), type);
146   }
147
148   /**
149    * Parses the response body to {@code type} using the parser negotiated from the response {@code Content-Type}.
150    *
151    * <p>
152    * When the header is absent or matches no registered parser and no default parser is configured, a
153    * <c>415 Unsupported Media Type</c> is thrown.  Use {@link #as(Parser, Class)} to force a specific parser,
154    * bypassing content negotiation.
155    *
156    * @param <T> The type to parse to.
157    * @param type The type to parse to. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
158    * @return The parsed body, or <jk>null</jk> if the response has no body.
159    * @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs reading the body or the body could not be parsed.
160    */
161   public <T> T as(Class<T> type) throws IOException {
162      return as(negotiatedParser(), type);
163   }
164
165   /**
166    * Parses the response body to {@code type} using the given parser.
167    *
168    * <p>
169    * This forces the supplied parser, bypassing the {@code Content-Type} negotiation performed by {@link #as(Class)}.
170    *
171    * <p>
172    * A parse failure is surfaced strictly as an {@link IOException} wrapping the underlying {@link ParseException};
173    * the malformed body is never returned to the caller.
174    *
175    * @param <T> The type to parse to.
176    * @param parser The parser to use. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
177    * @param type The type to parse to. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
178    * @return The parsed body, or <jk>null</jk> if the response has no body.
179    * @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs reading the body or the body could not be parsed.
180    */
181   public <T> T as(Parser parser, Class<T> type) throws IOException {
182      assertArgNotNull("parser", parser);
183      assertArgNotNull("type", type);
184      var body = response.getBodyAsString();
185      if (body == null)
186         return null;
187      try {
188         return parser.read(body, type);
189      } catch (ParseException e) {
190         throw ioex(e);
191      }
192   }
193
194   private Parser negotiatedParser() {
195      var h = response.getFirstHeader("Content-Type");
196      var ct = h == null ? null : h.value();
197      return response.getClient().getMatchingParser(ct).orElseThrow(() -> new UnsupportedMediaType(
198         "No parser matched the response Content-Type '%s' and no default parser is configured on the client.", ct));
199   }
200
201   /**
202    * Opens a token/record-streaming cursor over the response body using the given parser.
203    *
204    * <p>
205    * This forces the supplied parser, bypassing the {@code Content-Type} negotiation performed by
206    * {@link #asCursor(Class)}.
207    *
208    * <p>
209    * The cursor reads directly from the live response stream &mdash; the body is not buffered into memory.  The
210    * caller owns the returned cursor and the parent {@link RestResponse}; close them when done.
211    *
212    * <p>
213    * When {@code type} is (or extends) {@link TokenReader} the parser must implement {@link TokenReadable};
214    * otherwise it must implement {@link RecordReadable}.
215    *
216    * @param <T> The cursor type ({@link RecordReader}, {@link TokenReader}, or a concrete subtype).
217    * @param parser The parser that opens the cursor. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
218    * @param type The declared cursor type. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
219    * @return A cursor over the live response body. Never <jk>null</jk>.
220    * @throws IOException If the body is missing, the parser does not support the requested cursor surface, or the
221    *    produced cursor is not assignable to {@code type}.
222    */
223   @SuppressWarnings({
224      "unchecked", // The produced cursor is verified assignable to 'type' before the cast.
225      "resource"   // The cursor reads from the borrowed response stream; the caller closes the cursor / RestResponse.
226   })
227   public <T> T asCursor(Parser parser, Class<T> type) throws IOException {
228      assertArgNotNull("parser", parser);
229      assertArgNotNull("type", type);
230
231      var isToken = TokenReader.class.isAssignableFrom(type);
232      var supported = isToken ? parser instanceof TokenReadable : parser instanceof RecordReadable;
233      if (! supported)
234         throw ioex("Parser '%s' does not support the %s surface.", parser.getClass().getName(), isToken ? "token-reader" : "record-reader");
235
236      var stream = response.getBodyStream();
237      if (stream == null)
238         throw new IOException("Response has no body to open a cursor over.");
239
240      Object input = parser.isReaderParser() ? new InputStreamReader(stream, StandardCharsets.UTF_8) : stream;
241      var cursor = isToken
242         ? ((TokenReadable) parser).readTokens(input)
243         : ((RecordReadable) parser).readRecords(input);
244
245      if (! type.isInstance(cursor))
246         throw ioex("Parser '%s' produced cursor type '%s' which is not assignable to the declared type '%s'.", parser.getClass().getName(), cursor == null ? "null" : cursor.getClass().getName(), type.getName()); // HTT: cursor==null is defensive -- TokenReadable#readTokens/RecordReadable#readRecords are documented to always return a non-null cursor on success.
247
248      return (T) cursor;
249   }
250
251   /**
252    * Opens a closeable, cancellable cursor over a <c>text/event-stream</c> response body.
253    *
254    * <p>
255    * Reads the live response body as UTF-8 and dispatches one {@link SseEvent} at a time via the returned
256    * {@link SseEventReader}. The stream is not buffered into memory &mdash; events are parsed incrementally as bytes
257    * arrive, which is required for a long-lived Streamable-HTTP channel (see {@code juneau-rest-client-mcp}).
258    *
259    * <p>
260    * Closing the returned reader first closes the parent {@link RestResponse} (transport-layer cancel / release),
261    * then closes the reader itself.  This ordering is what makes the cursor <i>cancellable</i>: callers can stop
262    * consuming an open SSE channel at any time by calling {@link SseEventReader#close()}, including from another
263    * thread, without waiting for the server to finish sending events.
264    *
265    * <p>
266    * Transport-specific release behavior varies: this API guarantees that both the response and reader are closed in
267    * the above order, but the exact connection-release mechanism is determined by the active transport.
268    *
269    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
270    *    <li>This cursor is not thread-safe, except for using {@link SseEventReader#close()} as a cancellation signal from another thread.
271    *    <li>Mid-stream read failures are surfaced as {@link UncheckedIOException} from {@link SseEventReader#hasNext()} / {@link SseEventReader#next()} (per {@link SseEventReader} contract).
272    *    <li>Iterating after close throws.
273    * </ul>
274    *
275    * @return A cursor over the live response body. Never <jk>null</jk>.
276    * @throws IOException If the response has no body to open a stream over.
277    */
278   public SseEventReader asEventStream() throws IOException {
279      var stream = response.getBodyStream();
280      if (stream == null)
281         throw ioex("Response has no body to open an event stream over.");
282      return new ClosingSseEventReader(new InputStreamReader(stream, StandardCharsets.UTF_8), response);
283   }
284
285   /**
286    * An {@link SseEventReader} whose {@link #close()} also closes the parent {@link RestResponse}, so closing the
287    * cursor releases the underlying transport connection (cancellation) rather than merely stopping local reads.
288    */
289   private static final class ClosingSseEventReader extends SseEventReader {
290
291      private final RestResponse response;
292
293      ClosingSseEventReader(Reader in, RestResponse response) {
294         super(in);
295         this.response = response;
296      }
297
298      @Override /* Overridden from SseEventReader */
299      public void close() throws IOException {
300         try {
301            response.close();
302         } finally {
303            super.close();
304         }
305      }
306   }
307}
